definition: Multimodal treatment is an integrated care approach that uses more than one type of intervention together, such as psychotherapy, medication, and movement-based practices like Tai Chi. In this context, it means combining different methods so their roles and possible benefits can complement one another in mental health care.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “multimodal treatment” as an “integrated care approach”; it only states the review will synthesize literature to compare Tai Chi with pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy and discuss its “integrative potential within a multimodal treatment framework.”

The example list (“psychotherapy, medication, and movement-based practices like Tai Chi”) is only partially supported: the packet names psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy (supported) and Tai Chi (supported), but the “movement-based practices” phrasing is not stated directly.

The definition’s claims that the approach “means combining different methods so their roles and possible benefits can complement one another in mental health care” are not supported by the packet excerpt provided (it discusses “potential benefits, limitations, mechanisms,” but does not establish this specific ‘complement one another’ purpose/characterization as the meaning of multimodal treatment).
